Emma — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Jonas (Security) and Marissa (CS) so we can give a consolidated package.

High level answers up front:
- Deletion semantics: customers can request full tenant deletion or targeted deletion (datasets, snapshots, and model-derived artifacts). For tenant-scoped deletion we perform a coordinated multi-step workflow: mark-for-deletion -> export snapshot for forensics (48–72h retention in immutable store) -> delete active data and tokenized references -> purge KV caches and rotate short-term encryption keys. Our SOC 2 controls require a short immutable window to allow for investigations; we document and provide export artifacts as required.
- Scoped log redaction: we support automated redaction templates that remove or mask PII fields from application logs before retention/export. For forensic needs we provide redaction-reviewed exports and a short attestation describing the script and redaction verification steps.
- Exceptions: any deviation from standard retention is escalated to Security + Legal; approvals are tracked in our policy approval system with a signed approval artifact.

We're preparing two artifacts: a one-page "Deletion & Log Redaction Playbook" (PDF) and a SIG/CAIQ matrix where we've filled relevant rows for deletion and log handling. Jonas — can you attach the sample redaction output and the attestation text? Marissa — I'll add the commercial note about billing/SLAs.

Emma / Team — attaching the artifacts we discussed. Summary of technical details below, and the two attachments: sig-and-caik-matrix_2027-06.xlsx and sample-redaction-scripts.tar.gz (script + README + sample before/after).

Technical summary (concise):
1) Deletion semantics:
   - Scope: customer may request: (a) tenant wipe, (b) dataset-level deletion, (c) session-only purge.
   - Process: request -> validation -> create immutable forensic snapshot (if requested) stored in encrypted object storage with separate KMS key, retention TTL default 72h for snapshots unless legal hold requested -> proceed to data deletion steps which remove object references, metadata, and invalidate model-level pointers.
   - Proof: we produce deletion manifests (hashed object ids, timestamps) signed by system service account; sample manifest included in the playbook PDF.

2) Logs & redaction:
   - Application logs are segregated into operational logs (not customer content) and forensic traces (may contain customer identifiers). Forensic traces pass through a redaction pipeline: regex-based tokenization -> deterministic token mask -> verification run that samples N entries and asserts no raw PII remains.
   - For exports we provide both (a) redacted-for-consumption exports and (b) redaction-metadata (mapping of token ids to hashed values) if customer needs additional correlation. Access to mapping requires separate signed approval and is auditable.

3) Exception workflow / approvals:
   - Any retention shorter than our baseline (30d for request logs; 90d for some audit trails) requires: CSM + Security SPOC + Legal sign-off. Approvals are recorded in our Compliance Approval Ledger (we can export a signed PDF).

4) Artifacts for SIG/CAIQ:
   - Completed CAIQ rows related to LOG-3, DATA-1/2/3 and additional notes for customer-specific exceptions.
   - Sample deletion manifest and redaction verification report.

Billing/SLAs (Marissa to confirm): reduced retention or high-frequency forensic exports can incur additional engineering operational fees; they'll be detailed in the commercial note.

If this addresses Lumos' needs, we can prepare a short attestation (one paragraph) for their SIG and an exported XLS with the relevant CAIQ/CAIQ-lite answers. Emma — do you want us to include the internal deletion-manifest sample with hashed identifiers or would you prefer a sanitized sample?
